answers.question: How do I change the name shown on my account?
answers.shortAnswer: [Placeholder] LEAF shows the name from your directory record, so LEAF administrators can't edit it. Update your name with [team that owns the name record] and it will appear in LEAF after the next sync.
answers.steps:
1. Contact [team that owns the name record].
  2. Allow [timeline] for the change to reach LEAF.
  3. Sign out and back in to LEAF to see the update.

answers.question: Why is my old name still showing after I updated it?
answers.shortAnswer: [Placeholder] Name updates can take [timeline] to reach LEAF after the source record changes. If it's been longer than that, contact [team].
answers.steps:
1. Confirm the name is updated at [source of the name record].
  2. Sign out and back in to LEAF.
  3. If it still shows the old name after [timeline], contact [team].

answers.question: How do I get access to a LEAF site?
answers.shortAnswer: Access is usually granted by a site's own administrators, so contact the administrator of the site you need.
answers.steps:
1. Use Find a LEAF Site to locate the site.
  2. Contact that site's administrator and tell them what access you need.
  3. Ask them to confirm once access is added, then sign in again.

answers.question: Why can't I see or do something I could before?
answers.shortAnswer: Your permissions on a site come from the groups you belong to there. If something changed, ask that site's administrator to check your groups.
answers.steps:
1. Note the site and what you can no longer do.
  2. Contact that site's administrator.
  3. Ask them to confirm your group membership and restore it if it was removed.

answers.question: Why am I not getting LEAF emails?
answers.shortAnswer: Check your Junk and spam folders first. LEAF only emails when a request reaches a step set up to notify you, so no email can be normal.
answers.steps:
1. Check your Junk and spam folders.
  2. Ask the site administrator whether your step sends an email.
  3. If it should, ask them to confirm the email address on your account.

answers.question: How do I stop getting so many LEAF emails?
answers.shortAnswer: [Placeholder] Each LEAF site controls its own notifications, so ask that site's administrator to change them.
answers.steps:
1. Note which site and request sent the email.
  2. Ask that site's administrator to adjust the notification.

answers.question: How do I check the status of my request?
answers.shortAnswer: Open the request to see its current step. View My Requests on the Launchpad home page lists your LEAF National requests.
answers.steps:
1. Open the request from the LEAF site where you submitted it, or use View My Requests on the Launchpad home page.
  2. Check the current step shown on the request.
  3. Open the request history to see what has happened so far.

answers.question: Why hasn't my request moved?
answers.shortAnswer: A request moves when the person on its current step acts on it. LEAF can't speed that up, but you can follow up with them.
answers.steps:
1. Open the request and check its current step.
  2. Contact the person or group on that step.
  3. If the step looks wrong, contact the site administrator.
